compliance.cdm:
CDM 2015 REALITY FOR 115 VICARAGE ROAD (domestic client, multi-package, ~26-32 weeks):

1) The transfer mechanism. As a domestic client your duties under regs 4(1)-(7) and 6 are carried out for you (reg 7): by the sole contractor if there is one contractor, by the Principal Contractor (PC) where there is more than one contractor, or by the Principal Designer (PD) only if there is a WRITTEN agreement that the PD takes on the client duties. With 12-15 trade packages this is unambiguously a "more than one contractor" project, so a PC and PD must exist (reg 5).

2) What happens if nobody is appointed in writing. Reg 5(4) default: the designer "in control of the pre-construction phase" is deemed PD and the contractor "in control of the construction phase" is deemed PC. On a client-PM job with sequential labour-only packages this default is dangerous: no single trade is obviously "in control", every trade will deny it after an accident, and a client who is genuinely directing labour-only operatives on their own land starts to look like the person in control (and, for insurance purposes, like an employer - see insurance section). The client cannot be PC (domestic clients are outside the PC definition unless they elect into client duties under reg 7(3)), but the coordination vacuum is exactly what HSE criticises after incidents.

3) F10 notification. Threshold (reg 6): notifiable if the work will last more than 30 working days AND have more than 20 workers simultaneously, OR exceed 500 person-days. Domestic projects ARE notifiable if they hit the thresholds; the duty to notify transfers to the PC on a domestic job. This build never has 20 simultaneous workers, but 26-32 weeks = 130-160 working days; at an average of 3-4 operatives that is 450-600 person-days - genuinely borderline on the 500 person-day limb. The F10 is free and takes minutes on the HSE online portal: the pragmatic move is to have the shell-phase PC submit one at the start rather than argue about averages later.

4) Proportionate construction phase plan (CPP). Legally required for every project (reg 12 duty sits on the contractor/PC, not the domestic client) but HSE says explicitly it must be proportionate - for small domestic work a short plan via the free CITB "CDM Wizard" app or the HSE/L153 template is adequate. For this job a 4-6 page CPP should cover: project/contact details and hospital location; phase dates and trade sequence; site rules for a tight residential street (deliveries, skip, neighbour interface); welfare (toilet, water, drying - the client-PM must ensure this exists from day one); scaffold - designed, TG20:21 compliant, handover certificate, statutory 7-day inspections; excavations/piles - shoring or battering, no entry to unsupported trenches, spoil and rig standoff; temporary works (needles/propping during demolition and steel installation); services isolation before demolition; asbestos - a refurbishment/demolition survey BEFORE demolition is a legal prerequisite under CAR 2012 for a pre-2000 house; dust/noise; fire and first aid; who is PC in each phase.

5) The practical fix (do this, it costs nothing): a one-page signed appointment letter per phase. Letter 1: appoint the demolition/groundworks/masonry contractor (the shell contractor) as Principal Contractor for the shell phase, expressly accepting PC duties and the client duties under reg 7, with the CPP attached. Letter 2 at watertight: appoint the most site-present fit-out trade (typically the dryliner or first-fix carpenter/electrician firm) as PC for the fit-out phase. Letter 3: written agreement with the architect/SE to act as Principal Designer under reg 7(1)(c) for the pre-construction phase (many domestic architects resist taking the client duties - if so, let the PD function default to the PC and just keep the design risk information flowing: borehole report, SE drawings, asbestos survey handed to each PC as pre-construction information). Keep all letters, insurance certs and the CPP in one site file - that file is the entire CDM defence.

6) What HSE actually enforces on domestic sites. HSE does visit domestic jobs - usually drive-by triggered by visibly bad scaffolds or open excavations, plus targeted refurbishment inspection campaigns. Enforcement lands overwhelmingly on: falls from height (unguarded scaffolds, lack of edge protection, ladders, fragile roofs - the majority of construction fatalities are small-site falls), unsupported excavations (recent example: Greenlife Property Developments, prohibition notice on a 2.5m unshored garden excavation, breached it, fined £40,000 in January 2025), unsecured sites (public/child access), missing welfare, and silica/wood dust. Notices and Fee-For-Intervention invoices go to the contractor in control, but a self-managing client who ignores an obvious danger has no immunity - the domestic client exemption removes paperwork duties, not HSWA s.3 general duties when you direct the work. Practical priorities: pay for a proper scaffold with handover cert and weekly inspections, never let anyone enter an unsupported trench deeper than 1.2m, fence the site, provide a toilet, get the asbestos survey before demolition.
compliance.insurance:
INSURANCE INTERPLAY (this is the highest-consequence paperwork on the whole job):

1) Notify the existing home insurer BEFORE starting - in writing, and get their position in writing. Standard home insurance policies routinely restrict or void cover entirely when notified of structural works (and unoccupancy clauses of 30-60 days bite if the family moves out during the messy phases). Continuing to pay premiums does not mean you are covered. Assume the home policy will exclude damage arising from the works.

2) Buy a single self-build/renovation site policy in the CLIENT'S name for the full programme (buy 12 months minimum for a 26-32 week programme - policies are duration-rated, non-refundable, extendable). It must bundle: (a) CONTRACT WORKS - the new extension as it rises, plus materials on site and in transit; critical here because materials are client-supplied on trade accounts, so they are the client's property and no trade's policy covers them; (b) PUBLIC LIABILITY £5m - as self-managing client you control the site, so you need full project liability, not just landowner's liability; (c) EMPLOYERS' LIABILITY £10m - THE CRITICAL ONE: labour-only subcontractors and day-rate trades (most of this job) are treated as EMPLOYEES for insurance purposes - they work under your direction, often with client-supplied materials. If a price-work plumber falls off the scaffold, his claim lands on the person running the site. Every specialist self-build insurer (Protek, Self-Build Zone) includes EL for exactly this reason - do not economise on it; (d) EXISTING STRUCTURE cover - the second critical one: a blowtorch fire or a collapse during underpinning/steelwork takes out the whole house, not just the extension; the trade's £1m PL only responds if he was negligent and solvent. Optional but sensible: hired-in plant (mini digger, teleporter), site huts/tools, legal expenses.

3) Non-negligence / JCT 6.5.1-type cover. Public liability requires negligence; damage to the neighbour's property from subsidence, heave, vibration, collapse or removal of support (piling or trench-fill hard against the party wall boundary in a B14 terraced/semi street) can occur with nobody negligent - and then the liability is the building owner's personally, reinforced by the Party Wall Act position. 6.5.1-type cover is written in joint names, limits from £1m, premium always paid by the employer. As a self-managing client, buy it as an extension to the site policy (specialist self-build insurers offer it) rather than via a contractor. Typically a few hundred pounds; party wall surveyors increasingly ask whether it is in place. Essential if the borehole pushes you to piles.

4) 2026 market prices (indicative - get live quotes): Protek advertises self-build cover "from £228"; the working rule of thumb is 0.5-1% of build cost for the full project term. For ~£171k of works plus existing-structure cover on an occupied-plot extension, budget roughly £700-£1,700 total for 12 months, plus insurance premium tax, plus a few hundred for 6.5.1 cover. Protek, Self-Build Zone and BuildSafe are the standard three to tender (mirror the 3-quote discipline); Self-Build Zone has a dedicated extension product. A £250k/12-month project prices around £500+IPT as a published benchmark, so £171k plus existing structure sits comfortably in that band. Roughly £1,000-£2,000 all-in buys away the two uninsurable-by-trades catastrophic risks (existing house + injured labour-only tradesman) - the best stress-reduction per pound on the entire project.

5) Per-trade insurance checks (put in the tender pack, file the certificates): every trade supplies a current public liability certificate (£1m-£2m minimum; £5m for scaffolder and piling contractor) BEFORE starting; check expiry date covers their slot, and that the certificate actually covers the activity (groundworkers often have depth limits; heat-work exclusions matter for plumbers/roofers - cold-applied EPDM helpfully avoids hot works on the flat roof); genuine bona-fide subcontractors (scaffolder, piling firm, render firm, screed firm - firms that price, supply and self-direct) must carry their own PL and EL; the labour-only trades will often have thin or no cover - that is precisely what the client's site policy EL/PL is for, so verify what each trade is, rather than pretending everyone is bona fide. Keep a one-page register: trade, insurer, policy number, limit, expiry.
compliance.contracts:
CONTRACT FORMS - what actually protects a client-PM multi-package job:

1) The standard forms and where they fit. JCT Minor Works (MW): a 45-page contract assuming a contract administrator - the right tool for a single main contractor on a straightforward project, overkill and administratively wrong for 12-15 trade packages (you would need 15 CAs). JCT Home Owner contracts (with/without consultant): only 11 pages, plain-English, designed for homeowners - but designed for ONE builder doing the whole job, not trade packages. RIBA Domestic Building Contract: plain-English, HomeOwners Alliance-endorsed, digital completion, good where an architect administers - again single-contractor shaped. FMB small works contract: free but only via FMB-member builders, which price-work trades are not. Verdict used by experienced self-builders: none of the institutional forms fit a labour-only package structure; they use a tight 2-page trade order per package, and reserve a JCT Home Owner or RIBA Domestic contract for any single bundled package big enough to feel like a main-contract (e.g. if one firm takes demolition+groundworks+masonry+roof structure as a shell bundle - which also neatly solves the CDM Principal Contractor question for that phase). ContractStore's B153 Short Form of Trade Contract (an 18-paragraph letter-form agreement written specifically for self-builders engaging a roofer/bricklayer etc.) is a cheap purchasable template that matches this approach.

2) The 2-page trade order - the clauses that earn their place: (a) parties + site address + the trade's insurance certificate attached; (b) SCOPE SHEET - the single most important page: a bullet list of exactly what is and is not included, referencing a numbered DRAWINGS LIST with revision numbers ("Masonry to drawings 101 rev C, 102 rev B" kills the "I priced the old drawing" dispute); (c) FIXED PRICE, lump sum, and the VAT position stated in writing - for sub-threshold trades: "price is inclusive; contractor confirms he is not VAT registered"; for registered firms, VAT number on the order (protects against a surprise 20%); (d) STAGE PAYMENTS tied to physical milestones, never calendar dates (masonry: DPC / first lift / wallplate / gable completion; roof: trusses fixed / felt-batten / tiled) - always pay in arrears, never a deposit beyond invoiced materials; (e) RETENTION - 5% held until making-good and the relevant building control inspection passes, or 2.5% at practical completion + 2.5% at 3 months; retention is the only real post-completion leverage over a labour-only trade; (f) PROGRAMME - start date, duration, and (more useful than unrealistic damages clauses against small trades) a right to bring in others and back-charge if the trade abandons or stalls beyond 5 working days' written notice; (g) EXTRAS - a pre-agreed DAY RATE, and extras valid only if instructed in writing (text/WhatsApp suffices) and priced BEFORE execution - this single line prevents most end-of-job invoice shocks; (h) MAKING GOOD own damage, protecting the works of others, daily clean-up, debris to client skip; (i) who supplies what: client supplies materials on trade accounts; trade supplies consumables, fixings, own tools; (j) trade responsible for own tax/NI (domestic homeowners are NOT CIS contractors - pay gross, no CIS deductions, no HMRC scheme registration needed); (k) compliance deliverables named in the order (electrician: EIC + Part P notification; plumber/gas: Benchmark + Gas Safe notification; renderer: system warranty registration) with final payment conditional on handover.

3) Process discipline that does more than any clause: 3 written quotes per package against the same scope sheet (the tendering already assumed in the budget); a payment ledger (date, trade, milestone, amount, retention held); snag list walked jointly before the final payment of each package; every variation confirmed by text before it is built. On a job this size the paperwork burden is roughly one hour per package - the cheapest insurance on the project.
compliance.certs:
CERTS AND SIGN-OFF FLOW - who certifies what, and the closing pack:

1) Building control (the spine of the whole flow). Use full plans with Birmingham City Council LABC or a private Registered Building Control Approver - not a building notice, given piles/steels/attic trusses. Statutory inspection sequence for an extension: commencement notice; excavation/foundations inspected BEFORE concrete pour (with the borehole report and SE foundation design on site; if piled, the BC officer will want the pile design and the contractor's pile logs); DPC/oversite before the floor goes down; drainage before backfill plus an air/water test; structure - steels, padstones, floor and roof structure (trusses) before anything is covered; insulation/pre-plaster (including the warm-deck flat roof build-up); completion inspection issuing the COMPLETION CERTIFICATE. You must give notice at each stage and within 5 working days of completion (Regulation 16). Book inspections 48h ahead and never cover work before sign-off - the client-PM's core weekly admin task. The Completion Certificate is the keystone document every future conveyancer and lender asks for.

2) Electrics - Part P. Use an electrician registered with NICEIC/NAPIT (verify the registration number online before appointing): he self-certifies the notifiable work, issues an Electrical Installation Certificate (BS 7671) and his scheme lodges the Building Regulations Compliance Certificate with the local authority within 30 days - at no extra cost. An unregistered spark means paying building control for third-party inspection and pre-notification: on per-point pricing, registration is non-negotiable in the tender.

3) Gas. Any boiler/gas work by a Gas Safe-registered engineer, who self-certifies via the Gas Safe notification route; boiler commissioned with the Benchmark checklist completed (the manufacturer's warranty is void without it).

4) Structure. The SE certifies: foundation/pile design (reconciled to the borehole), steels and padstones, and any temporary works advice - ask at engagement for a final letter/certificate of design compliance and site-visit notes at the foundation and steel stages (cheap, and gold at resale). Attic trusses: the truss manufacturer's design office provides the design certificate and calculations free as part of supply - building control accepts the manufacturer's design package; file it with the SE's overall roof stability/bracing check.

5) Windows and the slider (Polish-supplied, non-FENSA fitter). No FENSA/CERTASS certificate will exist - and none is needed: new openings in an extension are certified through the extension's building regs approval and Completion Certificate, not FENSA (FENSA covers replacement windows in existing dwellings). Protect resale by filing the CE/UKCA marking and Declarations of Performance (U-values, safety glazing to doc K in critical locations) from the Polish manufacturer, and ensure the BC officer sees the spec at the insulation stage.

6) Roof and render warranties. EPDM: buy the membrane through a scheme (Permaroof/ClassicBond/Rubber4Roofs-type) using a trained/certified installer and REGISTER the warranty - typically 20 years on the membrane, activated by submitting completion photos and the order number; check transferability to a future buyer. Silicone render: manufacturer system warranties (K Rend/Weber/Parex class, typically 10 years) apply only when the FULL system (basecoat, mesh, beads, topcoat) is used and usually only via an approved applicator - specify the full system in the render package and get the warranty registration or, failing approved status, a written workmanship guarantee. Warranties that are never registered do not exist at resale.

7) THE CLOSING PACK (assemble as you go; digital folder + hard copy): planning decision notice + approved drawings; Building Regs full-plans approval + COMPLETION CERTIFICATE; party wall award(s) + schedule of condition; borehole/soil report; SE calcs, drawings and final compliance letter; pile logs/integrity results (if piled); truss design certificate + calcs; steel/connection details; EIC + Part P Building Regs Compliance Certificate; Gas Safe notification + Benchmark; drainage test record; EPDM registered warranty; render system warranty; window/door DoPs and UKCA docs; screed mix/UFH commissioning record; product datasheets for insulation build-ups; updated EPC; the site insurance policy documents; the CDM file (appointment letters + CPP) as evidence of a properly run project. Optional resale armour: a retrospective 10-year structural warranty (Protek/Self-Build Zone, roughly £1k-£2k for an extension) or a Professional Consultant's Certificate from the SE/architect - not required, but either silences lender questions about a no-main-contractor build. This pack is what converts a self-managed build from a conveyancing red flag into a documented asset.

ladder: (a) PURE SELF-PM (baseline): GBP 0 direct fee (~GBP 500-1,000 incidentals: software, printing, extra site insurance admin). Client time 20-30 hrs/wk for 26-32 weeks (NSBRC/Homebuilding confirm this range for self-managed builds). Savings retention: 100% of the ~GBP 34k-51k pool that trades-direct saves vs a main contractor on this GBP 171k job. Maximum stress; the client IS the contractor for sequencing, chasing, deliveries, BC call-outs and payment risk.

(b) WORKING FOREMAN (lead-trade uplift): Real but informal market practice - on domestic jobs the brickie gang leader, groundworker or carpenter commonly acts as charge-hand/'working foreman'; UK 2026 data shows a working-foreman premium exists (foreman day equivalents ~GBP 304-320 vs standard brickie GBP 240-320), i.e. an uplift of roughly GBP 30-70/day or +10-20% on their rate, negotiated at tender. On this job: uplift on ~90-110 site days through shell = GBP 3,000-7,000 (~2-4% of contract). They WILL take on: day-to-day sequencing of following trades, accepting/checking deliveries, setting out, site safety/tidiness, calling building control for their stages, first-line problem solving. They will NOT take on: tendering, contracts, vetting other trades' invoices/stage payments, design/spec decisions, procurement of finishes (windows, bathrooms, tiles), snagging other trades (conflict of interest), CDM paperwork. Client time drops to ~10-15 hrs/wk. Retention ~85-90%.

(c) FREELANCE SITE MANAGER / PART-TIME PM: 2026 freelance SM day rates GBP 240-500, residential domestic realistically GBP 280-400 (live August 2026 listings: GBP 240-260 Potters Bar, GBP 280-300 Bedford/Bolton, GBP 350-400 residential development; construction PM median much higher at GBP 470-600 but that is full-scope commercial). At 1 day/wk x 30 wks x GBP 325 = ~GBP 9,750; 2 days/wk = GBP 19,500-24,000 (6-14% of contract). Covers: programme/sequencing, trade chasing and booking, delivery scheduling, BC visit coordination, quality checks, informal valuation of stage payments. Find them via: retired SMs through local word of mouth and the NSBRC, LinkedIn 'freelance site manager Birmingham', CV-Library/Jooble freelance SM listings, MyBuilder/Checkatrade project-management category, Build It directory and specialist self-build PM firms (e.g. Samuel James-type practices, which quote ~5-10% of build cost or ~GBP 800/wk full-time - avoid the 10%/GBP 17k full-service tier). Client time ~5-10 hrs/wk (finishes procurement and decisions stay with client). Retention ~60-80% at 1 day/wk; one prevented sequencing error (GBP 3-5k) part-funds it.

(d) QS-LITE / EMPLOYER'S-AGENT-LITE for stage-payment vetting: fixed-fee market exists - initial high-level costing ~GBP 900; cost review GBP 2,000-5,000; ~2% of project value for fuller self-build QS service (~GBP 3,400 here); EA appointments from ~GBP 2,000+VAT; per-visit interim valuations ~GBP 250-500. On this job: GBP 1,500-3,500 fixed (~1-2% of contract) for monthly valuation visits + payment certificates over ~7 months. Saves only 2-3 hrs/wk of client time but removes the highest-stakes stress (overpaying ahead of work done, deposit exposure with price-work trades). Retention ~92-96%. Stacks cleanly on top of (a) or (b).

(e) SHELL PACKAGE (one builder to weathertight, client finishes): 2026 shell-only extension rates GBP 1,300-1,900/m2 ex VAT vs GBP 1,900-3,300/m2 turnkey (Build It/structuralengineercalcs). Shell phase of this job (demolition, foundations, cavity masonry, attic-truss roof + EPDM, windows/slider, render) is ~55-60% of the GBP 171k = GBP 95-105k trades-direct; a single shell contractor typically prices that at +10-15% = GBP 10,000-15,000 premium (single point of responsibility, their margin on the structure only, materials via their accounts). Client time ~5 hrs/wk during shell then back to 15-20 hrs/wk self-managing fit-out. Retention ~65-75%. Good fallback if no working-foreman candidate emerges at tender - note the client-supplied-windows saving (Polish-landed) usually dies under this model because shell builders want to supply the envelope.

(f) FULL MAIN CONTRACTOR (verify 20-30% claim): 2026 evidence supports ~15-25%, i.e. the claim is broadly right at the top end: residential MC pricing = overheads/prelims 10-20% + profit 5-10% ('10 and 10 rule'); Homebuilding/Build It data shows self-managing saves 17-25% vs appointing an MC, and 'a main contractor will typically charge around 20% for profit and overheads'. On this job: GBP 171k trades-direct becomes ~GBP 205,000-222,000, an extra GBP 34,000-51,000 - and the sub-VAT-threshold labour and client-supplied-materials advantages are also lost (MC adds 10-20% markup on materials and is VAT-registered on everything). Client time 2-5 hrs/wk. Savings retention ~0% - confirmed budget-killer.
market.bundling_evidence: NO-PREMIUM BUNDLES (often cheaper than splitting): (1) Roofer doing tiles + warm-deck EPDM + fascias/soffits + gutters in one visit - documented saving of GBP 700-2,000 because the second scaffold hire and second mobilisation disappear; roofline work priced marginally (e.g. ~GBP 445 for 24m of capping while already up there). (2) Groundworker doing drainage + slab + service trenches (+ patio sub-base for the later porcelain patio) - digger, driver and muck-away are already mobilised; splitting these re-charges plant each time. (3) Dryliner doing boarding + tape-and-joint to Level 4/5 - one trade, own materials logic, one mobilisation; a separate skim/finishing contractor re-prices access and prep. (4) Single brickie gang for both storeys including detailing - gang price per 1,000 bricks doesn't rise with scope. ALWAYS-ADD-MARGIN BUNDLES: (1) Combined M&E firms vs separate spark + price-work plumber - M&E firms are VAT-registered (instantly +20% on labour vs the sub-threshold sole traders this budget assumes) and add a coordination margin; per-point electrics + price-work plumbing direct is structurally cheaper. (2) Builder-supplied materials - standard UK markup 10-20% on merchant trade price, rising to 25-40% for specialist/urgent items (Screwfix community, MyBuilder, QuoteSmith all confirm); client-supplied on trade accounts avoids the whole layer, but expect labour-only quotes to be slightly higher to compensate. (3) Main contractor prelims/OH&P - 10-20% overhead + 5-10% profit on EVERYTHING including the trades you could have bought direct. (4) Turnkey/package premium - GBP 1,500-1,750/m2 turnkey vs GBP 800-950/m2 shell shows the finishing-stage management premium is the most expensive management money can buy; finishes are exactly where this client's auction-bathroom/clearance channels save the most.
market.tools: What experienced self-builders (BuildHub forum, trade app reviews) report actually reduces chasing: (1) ONE PRIMARY MERCHANT + call-off delivery calendar - a single credit account (Travis Perkins/Selco for structural bulk, or local MKM/Jewson branch with a named account manager) with materials ordered as phased call-offs against a weekly delivery calendar; free delivery typically above GBP 100-250 order value, GBP 30-80 below it. BuildHub consensus: keep a SECOND account (national + local independent) purely for price leverage and emergency stock - single-sourcing everything removes resilience. (2) WHATSAPP SITE GROUP WITH NORMS - one group, all trades in it; Friday 'next-week lookahead' post (who's on site, what's being delivered); photo of every element before it's covered (DPC, wall ties, cavity insulation, first-fix runs, screed prep); no money talk in the group (payments handled 1:1). Reported failure mode: it works 'up to a point' - hours get lost searching threads once 4+ trades overlap, which is exactly the fit-out stage. (3) STAGE-GATE PHOTO EVIDENCE TIED TO PAYMENTS - no stage payment released without the photo set + (if using rung d) the QS's nod; kills the biggest stress source (paying ahead of work). (4) SNAGGING APPS at finishes stage - Snaglist is the standout for this model because trades don't install anything (they open a link, see their snags, submit photo-evidenced completions); SnagX similar; Buildertrend-class platforms are overkill for one domestic job. (5) BUILDHUB.ORG.UK as the free experienced-self-builder helpdesk for sequencing questions - repeatedly cited as the highest-value zero-cost stress reducer.
market.recommendation: Buy delegation where GBP-per-stress-unit is best, not top-down. Recommended stack for 115 Vicarage Road: (1) Rung (b) working foreman - at tender, ask the groundworker and brickie gang leader to price a charge-hand role (+GBP 40-60/day) through demolition-to-weathertight; budget GBP 4,000-6,000. (2) Rung (d) QS-lite - fixed-fee monthly stage-payment vetting, budget GBP 2,000-3,000; this is the cheapest stress reduction per pound on the whole ladder. (3) Selective rung (c) - a retired/freelance site manager at ~GBP 325/day for 1 day/wk ONLY during the 8-10 week fit-out overlap (screed/first-fix/dryline/second-fix), budget GBP 3,000-4,000, sourced via NSBRC, LinkedIn Birmingham, or MyBuilder/Checkatrade PM listings - fit-out is where WhatsApp-only coordination breaks down. Total delegation spend ~GBP 9,000-13,000 (5-7.5% of contract), client hours fall from 20-30 to ~8-12/wk, and ~70-80% of the GBP 34-51k savings pool is retained. Reject: full-time PM at 10% (GBP 17k+), shell package (GBP 10-15k premium and it kills the Polish window saving) unless no working-foreman candidate emerges, and full main contractor (+GBP 34-51k, retention ~0% - the 20-30% claim verifies at 15-25% plus lost VAT/materials advantages, so effectively 20-30% all-in).

map_fixes: ATTACK 1 - Wallplate double-owned: draft puts the wallplate in both P2 (masonry) and P3 (carpentry). Classic dispute seed - if trusses rock, each blames the other. FIX: masonry gang beds, levels and straps the wallplate (they are on the scaffold at that level); P2's final milestone payment is released only on 'wallplate accepted in writing by the P3 carpenter' - a 10-minute check that converts the handoff into a signed gate.

ATTACK 2 - Cavity trays and the roof abutment orphan: nobody in the draft explicitly owns the retrofit cavity trays cut into the existing party-flank wall where the new roof abuts, and tray/flashing misalignment is a documented brickie-vs-roofer dispute (LABC guidance confirms trays above every opening and abutment). FIX: P2 owns ALL trays, DPCs, weeps and lintels including cut-in abutment trays with stop ends, drawn on one detail that also shows P4's lead flashing laps; joint photo sign-off of trays before the roofer starts and before scaffold strike.

ATTACK 3 - Threshold drain is a four-trade collision: the level-threshold ACO channel for the 4.8m slider touches P1 (drain connection), P3 (slider fit), P8 (screed FFL) and the patio. Draft leaves it homeless. FIX: architect/client issues ONE finished-floor-level datum sheet in every tender pack and a datum board is fixed on site day 1; P1 installs the channel body and drainage connection with the external drains; P8 screeds to the datum; the patio package fits the grating last and falls the porcelain away from the channel.

ATTACK 4 - Structural opening demolition in the wrong package: draft has all demolition in P1, but the break-out into the existing house needs needling/propping that belongs with the steel erection. If P1 demolishes and P2 erects steels, neither owns the props. FIX: split demolition - external structures to P1; break-out of the structural opening, temporary works (to SE's spec), steels, padstones and making good all move into P2 under one owner.

ATTACK 5 - UFH pipe ownership in the screed package: draft says 'screed day (+optional UFH pipe first)' - if the screeder lays pipe, the plumber disowns the manifold warranty and leak liability is contested under 55mm of screed. FIX: P6 plumber lays, clips and PRESSURE-TESTS the UFH loops and leaves them under pressure during the pour; the gauge photo + test certificate is the formal handoff; screeder pours over pressurised pipe and is not responsible for pipework. Plumber also owns the 21-day commissioning heat cycle (verified: start ~7 days post-pour, 25C for 3 days then step to max) with a named milestone payment - in the draft this task is an orphan and it voids floor warranties if skipped.

ATTACK 6 - Screed protection is unowned: verified aftercare is 24-48hr total closure, then board protection for site traffic, then boards OFF in time to dry (1mm/day, 6-8 weeks to 50mm). FIX: P8 includes laitance sanding and enforcing the 48hr closure; client buys protection boards on the materials account; P7 dryliner's FIRST contracted task is laying the protection; P9c flooring fitter carries out the moisture test (<75% RH) as his own acceptance gate so a failed reading is his problem to prove, not Mo's to argue.

ATTACK 7 - Render package materials plan kills the warranty: 'materials client-supplied' contradicts the verified warranty condition (full system + approved applicator only). FIX: P5 becomes the ONE supply-and-fix exception to the client-supplied-materials rule; still 3 quotes, final payment conditional on warranty registration. Sequencing verified: windows in FIRST, render up to frames with reveal beads, perimeter mastic seal LAST - mastic and making-good of reveals are written into P5's scope so no 'patching' dispute exists.

ATTACK 8 - Deck handoff between carpenter and roofer: warm-deck EPDM fails at the P3/P4 boundary if the deck, falls or firrings are wrong. FIX: P4 roofer issues a one-line written deck spec (board type, falls) at tender; P3 builds to it; P4 'accepts deck' by text before laying insulation/membrane - acceptance transfers responsibility.

ATTACK 9 - Scaffold has no home: P2, P4 and P5 all need it; if each prices their own you pay 2-3 mobilisations (~GBP 650/wk class item). FIX: new P0 client-direct attendance - one scaffold contract (bona fide sub, GBP 5m PL, TG20:21 design, handover cert, statutory 7-day inspections) with lift adaptations booked around P2->P4->P5; also in P0: welfare, fencing, skips, site insurance, merchant accounts. Scaffold strike date is a P5 milestone, not a scaffolder decision.

ATTACK 10 - P9 'finishes cluster' is a phase, not a package: four unrelated trades with no owner and the draft hides the patio inside it. FIX: split into P9a bathrooms (tiler tanking/tiling/sealing + P6 plumber setting sanitaryware - and auction-bought sanitaryware is INSPECTED on delivery since there is no returns channel; damage ownership transfers to the trade only after they accept it), P9b spray decoration (after Level-5 sign-off, moisture-checked), P9c flooring (own moisture test), kitchen fit as a P3 carpentry stage, and P10 porcelain patio as a separate post-completion package.

ATTACK 11 - P3 single-carpenter thread is a 26-week single point of failure: right instinct (one relationship, per-stage fixed prices) but wrong contract shape. FIX: each stage is a SEPARABLE fixed-price order with its own retention and an express right to re-let later stages after 5 working days' notice if he stalls - the relationship survives, the dependency doesn't.

ATTACK 12 - CDM/paperwork gaps confirmed: asbestos R&D survey is a legal prerequisite before any demolition (pre-2000 house); F10 is borderline on the 500 person-day limb so the shell PC submits one (free, minutes); PC appointment letters per phase (shell PC = P2 gang leader/foreman; fit-out PC = P7 dryliner or P3 carpenter, whoever is more site-present) plus a 4-6 page CITB-Wizard CPP; and the whole payment architecture stays: 2-page trade orders, physical-milestone stage payments in arrears, 5% retention (or 2.5+2.5), pre-agreed day rate for extras instructed by text only, compliance deliverables (EIC/Part P, Benchmark/Gas Safe, EPDM + render warranty registrations) as conditions of final payment.
final_packages: P0 CLIENT ATTENDANCES (not a trade): scaffold client-direct (TG20:21, GBP 5m PL, handover cert, 7-day inspections, ~6-8wk base hire + weekly top-ups), welfare/fencing/skips, self-build site policy + JCT 6.5.1-type cover, one primary merchant account (MKM/Travis Perkins) + one backup. Contract: hire agreements. Payment: monthly. Interface: scaffold lift changes booked by Mo around P2/P4/P5; strike only after render mastic complete.

P1 GROUNDWORKS + SUBSTRUCTURE: external demolition (post asbestos survey), excavation, piling attendance (piling firm client-direct with own design, PL GBP 5m, pile logs to BC), foundations, beam-and-block, drainage + soakaway + ducts, ACO threshold channel body set to FFL datum. Contract: 2-page trade order (B153-style), drawings listed by revision. Payment: demo clear / founds poured + BC pass / oversite / drains air-tested; 5% retention. CDM PC: P1 firm (appointment letter 1 + CPP). Interfaces: FFL datum board day 1; threshold channel body his, grating is P10's; leaves ducts marked and photographed.

P2 MASONRY SHELL + STRUCTURAL OPENING: both leaves, cavity insulation, ALL cavity trays/DPCs/weeps/lintels incl. retrofit abutment trays to party flank, break-out of opening with SE-spec propping, steels + padstones, wallplate bedded and strapped, telehandler day. Contract: trade order, gang price. Payment: DPC / first lift / joist bearing / wallplate ACCEPTED IN WRITING by P3 carpenter; 5% retention. CDM PC: gang leader as paid working foreman (letter 1b at P1 handover). Interfaces: tray/flashing detail shared with P4; photo of every tray before cover; hands scaffold to P4.

P3 CARPENTRY THREAD (one carpenter, separable stage orders): posi-joists; truss erection + bracing to manufacturer's design cert; flat-roof firrings + deck TO P4'S WRITTEN SPEC; window + 4.8m slider fitting; stairs; first fix; second fix (doors/skirting); kitchen fit. Contract: fixed price PER STAGE, right to re-let unstarted stages on 5 days' notice. Payment: per stage in arrears, retention per stage. CDM PC: no (except if chosen as fit-out PC). Interfaces: accepts wallplate from P2; deck accepted by P4 before membrane; window DoPs/UKCA docs filed for BC; kitchen after P9b decoration.

P4 ROOFING BUNDLE (one sub): tiling + dry-fix hips/verges, warm-deck EPDM cold-applied via scheme installer, fascia/soffit/RWG - one mobilisation, one scaffold use (verified GBP 700-2,000 saving vs splitting). Contract: trade order. Payment: felt-and-batten / tiled / EPDM + roofline done; final 10% on REGISTERED 20yr EPDM warranty. CDM PC: no. Interfaces: issues deck spec to P3 and accepts deck in writing; laps flashings over P2's trays per shared detail; RWG connects to P1's drainage.

P5 RENDER - SUPPLY-AND-FIX EXCEPTION: full silicone system (basecoat/mesh/beads/topcoat) by approved applicator for the 10yr system warranty; scope includes reveal beads, render to frames, perimeter mastic, making good. Contract: trade order naming the system. Payment: basecoat+mesh / topcoat; final on warranty registration. CDM PC: no. Interfaces: starts only after ALL windows + slider fitted; last trade on scaffold - his completion releases scaffold strike.

P6 M+E - TWO SEPARATE SUBS (no M+E firm margin, both sub-VAT sole traders if possible): (a) NICEIC/NAPIT electrician per-point - registration verified online before appointment; EIC + Part P scheme lodgement condition of final payment; (b) Gas Safe plumber price-work - incl. UFH loops laid + PRESSURE-TESTED (gauge photo = handoff to P8), boiler + Benchmark, UFH 21-day commissioning cycle as a named milestone, sanitaryware setting in P9a. Contract: trade orders per fix. Payment: first fix / second fix / certs delivered. CDM PC: no. Interfaces: first-fix photo walk with Mo before P7 boards.

P7 DRYLINING: tack, tape-and-joint, Level 5 zones per marked drawing; FIRST TASK = lay client-supplied protection boards over screed (after 72hr cure). Contract: trade order, own materials logic (boards/compound client account). Payment: boarded / jointed / Level 5 signed. CDM PC: YES - fit-out phase PC (appointment letter 2 at weathertight) unless P3 carpenter is more present. Interfaces: boards only after M+E photo sign-off; Level 5 sign-off gates P9b sprayer.

P8 SCREED: liquid screed over pressurised UFH to FFL datum; includes laitance sanding and enforcing 48hr closure. Contract: supply-and-fix day price. Payment: single payment on pour + datum check, small retention to laitance sand. CDM PC: no. Interfaces: pours ONLY against plumber's pressure-test cert; drying clock (1mm/day) drives P9c date; protection on at 72hr (P7), off in time to dry.

P9a BATHROOMS: tiler (tanking, tiling, sealing) + P6 plumber sets sanitaryware. Client-supplied auction/clearance sanitaryware inspected and accepted ON DELIVERY (no returns channel); trade accepts condition before touching it. Payment: per room complete + sealed. Interfaces: tanking before tiling photo; silicone by tiler, not plumber.

P9b SPRAY DECORATION: mist + finish coats after Level 5 sign-off and moisture check. Payment: per floor/zone. Interfaces: before P3 second-fix finals and kitchen fit; sprayer masks, P7 makes good own joints.

P9c FLOORING: fitters carry out OWN moisture test on screed (<75% RH) as acceptance - a failed reading is theirs to evidence. Payment: on completion per zone. Interfaces: protection lifted 2 weeks prior to dry; thresholds meet slider channel at datum.

P10 PORCELAIN PATIO (post-completion, separate tender): sub-base ideally dug/stoned by P1 while plant is mobilised (priced as P1 option), porcelain laid off the same FFL datum, threshold grating fitted, falls away from house. Payment: on completion. Interfaces: does not obstruct soakaway; protects render base bead.
verdict.delegation: RECOMMENDED RUNG: the STACK, not a single rung - (1) WORKING FOREMAN (rung b): at P1/P2 tender, ask the groundworker and brickie gang leader to price a charge-hand role at +GBP 40-60/day through demolition-to-weathertight (~90-110 site days): sequencing following trades, checking deliveries, setting out, calling BC for their stages, first-line problem solving, and holding the shell-phase CDM PC appointment. Budget GBP 4,000-6,000. (2) QS-LITE (rung d): fixed-fee monthly stage-payment vetting + payment certificates over ~7 months, GBP 2,000-3,000 - the cheapest stress-per-pound on the ladder; it removes the highest-stakes risk (paying ahead of work) and gives the ruthless-negotiator client an independent number to negotiate FROM. (3) SELECTIVE FREELANCE SM (rung c): ~GBP 325/day, 1 day/week ONLY during the 8-10 week fit-out overlap (screed/first-fix/dryline/second-fix) where WhatsApp coordination demonstrably breaks down; GBP 3,000-4,000 via NSBRC/LinkedIn Birmingham/Checkatrade PM listings. TOTAL DELEGATION: GBP 9,000-13,000 (5-7.5% of contract). Mo keeps the two things he is best at and that save the most money - tendering/negotiation and finishes procurement (Polish windows, auction bathrooms) - and sheds daily chasing. REJECTED: full-time PM at ~10% (GBP 17k+, buys nothing Mo can't do better himself at tender); shell package (GBP 10-15k premium AND kills the Polish-window saving because shell builders insist on supplying the envelope); main contractor (+GBP 34-51k, retention ~0%, confirmed budget-killer - the 20-30% claim verifies at 15-25% headline plus lost VAT and materials advantages, so ~20-30% all-in).
procurement_calendar: WK -10 to -8 (pre-start, longest-lead first): ORDER THE 4.8m ALUMINIUM SLIDER + Polish windows - verified the slider is the true critical-path item at 10-16 weeks (Polish window production 4-6 weeks); needed on site ~wk 10-12, so it must be ordered before ground is broken. Also: asbestos R&D survey booked; party wall notices served (s.6 adjacent excavation - allow 2 months for awards if dissent); borehole + SE foundation design commissioned; Building Control full plans submitted (LABC or RBCA).

WK -8 to -6: tender site insurance (Protek / Self-Build Zone / BuildSafe, GBP 700-1,700 + 6.5.1 cover) - policy must incept BEFORE demolition; notify home insurer in writing; tender P1 + P2 against scope sheets WITH the working-foreman uplift question; appoint QS-lite; open primary + backup merchant accounts.

WK -6 to -4: piling firm tendered and booked if borehole demands it (2-3 days on site, GBP 4.5-8k class, own design to SE); scaffold 3 quotes; TRUSS DESIGN started with manufacturer now - manufacture is only 5-10 working days but design + SE bracing check + BC sign-off is the real lead; steels enquiry to fabricator.
WK -2: award P1, P2; sign PC appointment letter 1 + CPP; delivery calendar v1 issued; skip/welfare/fencing ordered; F10 submitted by shell PC.

WK 0-2 (START ON SITE - demo/groundworks): order steels (2-3 wk fabrication) against SE finals; press the truss ORDER button once wallplate date is forecast (delivery wk 7-8); tender P4 roofing bundle + P5 render (approved applicators only).

WK 3-5 (masonry rising): order roof tiles, dry-fix kit, EPDM scheme kit, fascia/RWG; book scaffold lift adaptations; tender P6 (spark per-point + plumber price-work) and P7 dryliner; START WATCHING bathroom auctions/clearance - buy when right, store (garage), inspect on delivery.

WK 6-9 (wallplate/trusses/roof): trusses delivered + erected; windows/slider arriving - book P3 fitting stage; confirm P8 screeder + UFH materials (manifold, pipe, insulation) ordered; kitchen survey + order placed ~wk 8-10 (6-8 wk lead for wk 18-20 fit).
WK 10-13 (weathertight): render starts after last window in; PC letter 2 signed (fit-out PC); order plasterboard/compound call-off; flooring shortlisted (order held until screed moisture forecast).
WK 14-17: first fix M+E; screed poured ~wk 15-16 (drying clock starts: 1mm/day); UFH commissioning wk 16-19; order flooring for ~wk 22-24; tender P10 patio for post-completion.

WK 18-26: dryline/tape-joint; spray decoration; bathrooms; second fix; kitchen fit; BC completion inspection booked wk 25-26; retention releases begin; closing pack assembled continuously (certs, warranties registered, DoPs filed).
verdict.weekly_routine: MO'S WEEK (steady state ~6-8 hrs, peaks ~10-12 in tender bursts wk -8 to 2 and fit-out wk 14-22): SUNDAY 60-90 min - payment ledger update, next-week lookahead posted to the single WhatsApp site group (who's on site, what's delivering), delivery calendar call-offs emailed to merchant. MONDAY 30 min - confirm deliveries + scaffold/BC bookings (BC inspections booked 48h ahead - never let work be covered unsigned). MIDWEEK 60-90 min - ONE site walk with the working foreman (shell) or freelance SM (fit-out): photo the stage-gate evidence (trays, ties, first-fix runs, pressure gauge, deck acceptance), check against drawings list. FRIDAY 45-60 min - review QS-lite valuation or photo set, release stage payments 1:1 (never in the group), log retentions, confirm any extras were priced-by-text BEFORE execution. MONTHLY +1-2 hrs - insurance register check (cert expiries), closing-pack filing, BuildHub forum for any sequencing query. TENDER BURSTS +3-4 hrs/wk - Mo personally runs every 3-quote tender and negotiation (his strength, and where the money is) and all finishes procurement: Polish window spec calls, bathroom auction watching, tile/kitchen buying. What Mo NEVER does: chase trades daily, accept deliveries, sequence subbies on site, argue stage valuations without the QS number.
verdict.totals: TOTAL MANAGEMENT COST: delegation stack GBP 9,000-13,000 (foreman 4-6k + QS-lite 2-3k + fit-out SM 3-4k) + site insurance incl. existing-structure, EL/PL and 6.5.1 cover GBP 1,300-2,200 + incidentals (CPP/printing/snag app/protection boards) ~GBP 500 = GBP 10,800-15,700 all-in, say ~GBP 13,000 central. SAVINGS RETAINED: main-contractor route on this job = GBP 205,000-222,000 (+GBP 34,000-51,000 over the 171k trades-direct plan, verified at 15-25% OH&P plus lost sub-VAT labour and client-materials advantages). Self-managed with the stack = GBP 171k + ~13k = ~GBP 184,000, retaining GBP 21,000-38,000 (central ~GBP 30,000) of the savings pool = roughly 70-75% retention, while Mo's hours fall from the 20-30/wk of pure self-PM to ~6-8/wk steady state. The package-map fixes are free but real money: one scaffold contract instead of three mobilisations (~GBP 1-2k), the roofing bundle (~GBP 0.7-2k), P1 doing the patio sub-base while plant is mobilised, and the interface gates (wallplate acceptance, pressure-test handoff, deck acceptance, warranty-conditional finals) whose value is the GBP 3-5k dispute that never happens. Insurance is the best stress-per-pound buy on the project; the QS-lite is second.
